**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — Section 6.1 (¶p0037)**

Contrary to the planner's "likely absent" hint, the document does contain a Customer-side restrictive covenant, in the "6. Exclusivity" block:

- **Section 6.1** bars *the Company* from participating in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products **or products substantially similar** to them, expressly including competitor lines (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled "and companies similar"). That is a field-of-use restriction on our own channels, brands and sourcing — outside the playbook position.
- Term-only scope and the closeout carve-out (6.2) are helpful, but the "substantially similar / similar companies" language is effectively undefined competitive scope.
- **Section 6.3** (two-year post-term restriction on HDI) binds the counterparty and benefits us — left untouched.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** delete the Company-side covenant from 6.1 while preserving HDI's exclusive right to use the "Deerskin" brand for the self-contained site, so the core bargain survives. The comment offers the fallback: restriction limited to Deerskin Products only, during the term, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
